name: MonarchAiThread
title: AiThread
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn (reverseLayout = true) composing MonarchAiMessage, MonarchAiContextDivider, MonarchAiThinkingIndicator, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButton
summary: The scrolling list of an AI conversation: messages oldest first with day labels, pinned to the newest, with Jump to latest, Load earlier, a thinking indicator, connection notices and one announcer for the whole conversation.
whenToUse: The message area of an assistant screen, above a MonarchAiPromptInput, fed from a MonarchAiConversation.
whenNotToUse: For person-to-person chat use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For one answer without a conversation use MonarchAiMessage or MonarchAiStructuredAnswer on their own.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiThread(messages: List<MonarchAiConversationMessage>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(), status: MonarchAiConversationStatus = MonarchAiConversationStatus.Idle, error: MonarchAiConversationError? = null, offline: Boolean = false, queuedCount: Int = 0, slow: Boolean = false, hasEarlier: Boolean = false, loadingEarlier: Boolean = false, daySeparators: Boolean = true, timeZone: String? = null, nowMillis: Long? = null, announces: Boolean = true, announceIntervalMillis: Long = 1_000L, labels: MonarchAiThreadLabels = MonarchAiThreadLabels(), onStop: (() -> Unit)? = null, onLoadEarlier: (() -> Unit)? = null, jumpIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, message: @Composable LazyItemScope.(message: MonarchAiConversationMessage, context: MonarchAiThreadMessageContext) -> Unit = { item, context -> MonarchAiMessage(message = item, announces = context.announces, timeZone = timeZone) })
class MonarchAiThreadMessageContext(index: Int, isLast: Boolean, announces: Boolean)

class MonarchAiThreadLabels(label: String? = null, jumpToLatest: String? = null, newMessages: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, loadEarlier: String? = null, loadingEarlier: String? = null, thinking: String? = null, responseComplete: String? = null, responseStopped: String? = null, error: ((message: String) -> String)? = null, codeBlock: String? = null, today: String? = null, yesterday: String? = null, offline: String? = null, offlineQueued: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, sendingQueued: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, slow: String? = null)

options.name: messages
options.description: The visible conversation, oldest first: MonarchAiConversation.messages.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state. Index 0 is the bottom row, so firstVisibleItemIndex == 0 means the newest message is in view.

options.name: contentPadding
options.description: Padding around the messages inside the scrolling area.

options.name: status
options.description: Submitted shows the thinking indicator; Submitted and Streaming make Escape call onStop; Stopped ends the announcement with "Response stopped".

options.name: error
options.description: Announced assertively as "Error: <message>" when the newest message has no error part of its own.

options.name: offline
options.description: Shows the offline notice under the messages.

options.name: queuedCount
options.description: How many messages wait for the connection; named in the offline notice, and once online shows "Back online. Sending N queued messages…".

options.name: slow
options.description: Shows "This is taking longer than usual. Still working…" while a reply is submitted or streaming.

options.name: hasEarlier
options.description: Older messages exist. With onLoadEarlier, "Load earlier messages" is the top row.

options.name: loadingEarlier
options.description: The load button shows progress and "Loading earlier messages…" as its state.

options.name: daySeparators
options.description: A MonarchAiContextDivider day label above the first message of each calendar day.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: IANA zone of the day labels and of the default messages' times. null is the device zone.

options.name: nowMillis
options.description: Reference time for Today and Yesterday, epoch milliseconds UTC. null reads the clock.

options.name: announces
options.description: The thread announces for the whole conversation and tells each message not to; false lets each message announce itself.

options.name: announceIntervalMillis
options.description: Least time between two polite announcements while a reply streams.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Called by the Escape key inside the thread while a reply is running.

options.name: onLoadEarlier
options.description: Loads older messages; prepend them to messages. The view does not move.

options.name: jumpIcon
options.description: Icon before "Jump to latest". Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: empty
options.description: Shown instead of the list when there are no messages, no older ones and no submitted reply, for example a MonarchAiWelcome.

options.name: message
options.description: Draws one message, given its index, whether it is the newest and whether it should announce itself.

states.name: pinned
states.description: While the newest row is within 48dp of the bottom, a new message or the thinking indicator scrolls into view and a growing reply stays anchored at the bottom.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: New messages do not move the view; a "Jump to latest" button over the bottom of the list counts them ("2 new messages") and scrolls back, animated unless animations are off.

states.name: submitted
states.description: A MonarchAiThinkingIndicator is the bottom row, and "Thinking…" is announced once.

states.name: streaming
states.description: The reply is read out in whole sentences, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped" when it ends.

states.name: earlier
states.description: "Load earlier messages" (MonarchLoadMore) is the top row; while loading it shows progress.

states.name: offline / sending / slow
states.description: One MonarchInlineNotice under the list, offline first: warning tone for the connection, neutral for a slow reply.

states.name: error
states.description: An error no message shows is announced assertively; nothing is drawn for it.

states.name: empty
states.description: The empty content replaces the list.

appearance: The thread has no surface of its own: it shows on the screen's background. Messages, day labels, the thinking indicator and the load button keep their own roles; the notice uses the warning or neutral tone of MonarchInlineNotice, and the jump button is a small secondary MonarchButton. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web renders a scrolling div with role=log, measures rows and windows them itself after 200 messages (virtualizeAfter, keepLast, estimatedMessageHeight). On Android the LazyColumn composes only the rows on screen, so those parameters do not exist; reverseLayout keeps the newest at the bottom and LazyListState.requestScrollToItem follows new rows while the person is at the bottom. The web's renderMessage and messageProps are one trailing message lambda; pass MonarchAiMessage's parameters there. The web's locale prop is the configuration locale. The web reads Markdown tables as "Table"; this announcer names code blocks, drops heading and bold marks and reads the rest as text, so there is no table label. The web draws warning and clock glyphs in the notice; Monarch bundles no icons, so the notice's tone and text carry the meaning. The composer is not part of the thread on either platform: put a MonarchAiPromptInput under it. iOS has not covered this entry yet. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: Day labels are MonarchAiContextDividers, read as one element: "Today", "Yesterday" or the date.

With announces, one always-present polite live region says "Thinking…" when a reply is submitted, reads a reply that arrives while the thread is shown in whole sentences at most once per announceIntervalMillis, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped"; replies that were already finished are not read.
The messages get announces = false from the context, so streamed text is not read token by token.
A conversation error that no message shows is announced from an always-present assertive live region.
The offline, sending and slow notices sit outside the list in an always-present polite live region.
"Jump to latest" and "Load earlier messages" are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; the jump button reads its count of new messages with its label.
Escape inside the thread calls onStop while a reply is submitted or streaming.
Jumping uses scrollToItem instead of an animation when animations are off.
edgeCases: Give the thread a bounded height; it cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent.
Message ids must be unique and stable: they are the lazy list keys.
Older messages prepended to messages keep the view where it is.
A message whose createdAt is not an ISO 8601 time gets no day label, and the next message starts a new day, as on the web.
The empty content shows only when there are no messages, nothing to load and no submitted reply.
Offline wins over the sending and slow notices; slow shows only while a reply is running.

examples.title: A finished turn
Older history, a custom message and the offline notice
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchAiThread(
    messages = messages,
    modifier = Modifier.height(MonarchTheme.spacing.space24 * 3),
    offline = true,
    queuedCount = 1,
    hasEarlier = true,
    loadingEarlier = loading,
    timeZone = "Europe/Madrid",
    onLoadEarlier = { loading = true },
) { message, context ->
    MonarchAiMessage(
        message = message,
        announces = context.announces,
        timeZone = "Europe/Madrid",
        showActions = context.isLast,
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the copy, edit and regenerate buttons of a message only on hover and focus. A phone has no hover, so the buttons are always shown under each message (copy under the person's message; copy and regenerate under the assistant's). The web composer is drawn as a Send a message button and a Stop button; on Android the composer is the prompt field with its Stop button inside it, the field the person types in.
parityExceptions.convention: no hover on a touch device: message actions are always visible (Material)
